subject: Annotate cpg N and S shores and shelves

messages.author: b96f540af97297dc
messages.subject: Annotate cpg N and S shores and shelves
parts: Is there anyway of annotating cpg shores N and S (i.e before or after the island) and the shelves (2000bp before/after the shore)?  I want to produce diff meth info based on these, like this http://www.plosgenetics.org/article/fetchObject.action?uri=info:doi/10.1371/journal.pgen.1003572.g001&representation=PNG_L

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Annotate cpg N and S shores and shelves
parts:
You can do that using genomic ranges, you have to read in the CpG islands as GRanges, calculate shores and shelves, or use the function readFeatureFlank() function in methylKit, which will read CpG islands and shores, than you have to calculate shelves out of shores. You will have then 3 GRanges CpGi, shores and shelves. Then use findOverlaps() or %over% to see get which ones of the DMR/DMCs overlap with those annotations.
http://al2na.github.io/compgenr/genomic_intervals/granges.html

Best,
Altuna

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] Annotate cpg N and S shores and shelves
parts:
make a 3 column matrix, number of rows equal to your number of DMRs (see ?matrix). initialize with 0 or FALSE, and use %over% in GenomicRanges to create a logical vector

mat[ DMR %over% CpGi,1]=1
mat[ DMR %over% shores,2]=1
mat[ DMR %over% shelves,3]=1
colnames(mat)=c("CpGi","shores","shelves")

mat is your initialized matrix, DMR, CpGi, shores and shelves are GRanges objects. You can coerce methylKit objects to GRanges, see vignette.

Best,
Altuna

parts:
Hi Altuna,

I had a couple questions about a bit of code that you shared via your github.

What is the purpose of equalizing the coordinates? Also, I'm confused at that code. 

# end of the + strand genes must be equalized to start pos
end(tss.gr[strand(tss.gr)=="+",])  =start(tss.gr[strand(tss.gr)=="+",])
# startof the - strand genes must be equalized to end pos
start(tss.gr[strand(tss.gr)=="-",])=end(tss.gr[strand(tss.gr)=="-",])

Is this a typo? I assume you meant to say:

end position on "+" strand set to start position on "-", and start on "-" strand is set to end position on "+".

Appreciate any clarification.

Thanks,
Stephen
